author: B

components.title: Compute remaining work
components.what: Find the combined filling rate of pumps A and B, calculate how much of the tank they fill in 4 hours, and determine the fraction remaining after pump A is switched off.

components.title: Calculate and round time
components.what: Use pump B's rate alone to find the additional time needed for the remaining fraction, convert the result from hours to minutes, and round to one decimal place.

components.title: Format the response
components.what: Show brief working, then end with exactly one line of the form FINAL: <answer>, using digits only with a decimal point and no units on that final line.

log.author: B
log.draft:
Pump A’s rate is \(1/10\) tank/hour, and pump B’s rate is \(1/9\) tank/hour.

Combined rate:
\[
\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{9}=\frac{19}{90}
\]

In 4 hours, they fill:
\[
4\times\frac{19}{90}=\frac{38}{45}
\]
So the remaining fraction is:
\[
1-\frac{38}{45}=\frac{7}{45}
\]

Pump B alone needs:
\[
\frac{7}{45}\div\frac{1}{9}=\frac{7}{5}=1.4\text{ hours}
\]
\[
1.4\times60=84.0\text{ minutes}
\]

FINAL: 84.0

answer:
